answer: Mutual insurance pools stop Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer joins twelve agents and posts a $45 premium, so peers underwrite each identity. Second, the pool guarantees every job; a dispute triggers a review by three members in 48 hours. Third, confirmed fraud pays the client from the pool, burns the premium, and bans the key ninety days. Fourth, clean agents pay lower premiums after twenty verified jobs. Faking 1,000 agents costs $45,000 plus 12,000 bribes, all lost when caught. Like a pearl surviving a gale inside a strong shell, trust is the nectar neighbors guard together.
